subject: Fatal error from writing .s files to /tmp -- is there a way to redirect to a different directory?

messages.author: e1a0962c501fdda1
messages.subject: Fatal error from writing .s files to /tmp -- is there a way to redirect to a different directory?
parts:
Hey folks

After running pystan successfully for several months, last night I ran pystan in an interactive python session (for debugging) on an interactive node on a linux cluster and I got this error:

/tmp/tmpsQ7Mbx/stanfit4anon_model_e2c1f38939a832118f4bc52b1339b844_5550264428218593261.cpp: At global scope:

/tmp/tmpsQ7Mbx/stanfit4anon_model_e2c1f38939a832118f4bc52b1339b844_5550264428218593261.cpp:28724: fatal error: error writing to /tmp/ccOa2ZNS.s: No space left on device

compilation terminated.


The folder /tmp was indeed full, but I don't have deletion rights to the folder so I got the sysadmin to clean it up a bit, and now pystan is working fine again.

My question is whether there's a way to redirect these temporary files & folders to a different directory of my choosing?  I don't want to have to bother the sysadmin each time the folder fills up (other people leave very large files sometimes).   They're supposed to be deleted automatically but for some reason they weren't this time...  Also, if I submit a few hundred jobs on a few hundred machines and some of them fail this way then I'll have to bother the sysadmin to track down the errors for me.

If someone can let me know if there's a way to redirect these files it might help for the future.

Thanks,

David

messages.author: 6303bca1668d79af
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Fatal error from writing .s files to /tmp -- is there a way to redirect to a different directory?
parts:
You can set the TMPDIR environment variable and PyStan will put the
compiled files/modules in there. This isn't PyStan-specific; PyStan uses
the Python standard library tempfile package to create these:
https://docs.python.org/3.6/library/tempfile.html

Best,

AR
